items.title: Jev: Bounded semantic judgments for messy text
items.content_text: Imagine that you are building the software for a coffee shop. A customer types: "One big coffee with lots of milk, but no normal milk, please." A barista might guess that the customer means a large latte with plant-based milk. The application needs a more careful process. "Big" probably means large , but "no normal milk" does not tell us whether the customer wants oat, soy, or almond milk. An intelligent component can identify the likely intent. The cache has access latencies ranging from a few processor cycles to 10 or 20 cycles, rather than the hundreds of cycles needed to access RAM. items.title: Examining Huge Pages or Transparent Huge Pages Performance
items.content_text: All modern processors use page-based mechanisms to translate the user-space processes virtual addresses into physical addresses for RAM. The pages are commonly 4KB in size, and the processor can hold a limited number of virtual-to-physical address mappings in the Translation Lookaside Buffers (TLB). The number of TLB entries ranges from tens to hundreds of mappings. This limits a processor to a few megabytes of memory it can address without changing the TLB entries.
